audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer labels this HARD while scoring every one of the seven stages 8/10 for Akshan and rating difficulty 4/10 with a "Free harass lane" TL;DR. On the content side, five of the seven whys (0, 3, 4, 5, 6) argue Galio wins the stage they are attached to, while the win array gives all seven to Akshan.
audit.why: The Galio-side mirror settled this lane as HARD 8/10 for Galio with Akshan owning every stage, so the chart is not the thing to change — the label and the contradicting whys are. Mechanically it holds up: Avengerang reaches 850 on a 9s rank-1 cooldown and Galio has no way to close on foot once Justice Punch is spent.
audit.corrected: diff set to FAV so it agrees with the 4/10 rating and the all-Akshan chart, and the five contradicting whys rewritten to give the Akshan-side reason for their own stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hero's Entrance is called a "global R" in four strings (spikes[1], wants.foe[2], whys[4], late).
audit.why: Its range is 4000/4750/5500 — long, but not global, and at rank 1 that is roughly a lane and a half, not the map. Akshan's own Going Rogue has 5500 range on its roam, so at rank 1 Galio's ultimate does not even out-reach it. Calling it global tells you the roam is uncontestable when it is not.
audit.corrected: All four strings now give the real 4000-at-rank-1 reach and note that Going Rogue matches it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page said Justice Punch "locks your Heroic Swing in place", and whys[0] credited Galio with "Q (Winds of War) sustain". Neither Heroic Swing's terrain requirement nor Comeuppance's blocking rule appeared anywhere.
audit.why: Riot's Heroic Swing description says he "gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain" — so Justice Punch's collision cancels the swing outright rather than locking you in it. Winds of War is two windblasts converging into a damage-over-time tornado with no healing in its description at all. And Comeuppance deals its damage "to the first champion, minion, or structure hit", so any minion in the line eats the whole ultimate — that is the level-6 rule and it was missing. Shield of Durand's reduction is also weighted toward magic damage, and every point of Akshan's damage is physical.
audit.corrected: Justice Punch's 11s cooldown and its collision-cancels-the-swing behaviour are stated across the cooldown block, the do's, the don'ts and the interactions report; the fabricated Q sustain is gone; the minion-blocks-Comeuppance rule is now in the Level 6 stage.

edits.before: This is where it slips. His W (Shield of Durand) is a channeled damage-reduction that releases a taunt — pop it and your passive second-shot, your Avengerang, and your Heroic Swing autos all get blunted, then he taunts you out of the swing and E-knocks you up. At 6 his E (Justice Punch) into W taunt is a gap-close lock you cannot kite, and his global R (Hero's Entrance) means he ult-roams bot the second you back off. Note he often over-builds MR here — wasted against your AD — so your Youmuu's burst still hurts; the problem isn't his defenses, it's that one taunt chain trades your whole life for it. Trade only on your Q cooldown when his W is on cooldown.
edits.after: This is the fight to get right. His W (Shield of Durand) is a channeled damage-reduction that releases a taunt on 18s at rank 1 — but the reduction leans against magic, and every point of your damage is physical, so it blunts far less here than against a mage. The real danger is his E (Justice Punch): colliding with a champion knocks you off Heroic Swing, so a punch thrown into your swing cancels it outright and the taunt follows. Fight beside a wall so the swing has terrain within 800 to grapple, and trade on your 9s Avengerang while his 11s punch is down. At 6, remember Comeuppance stops on the first minion or champion in the line — keep the shot clear before you channel.

edits.before: You lose the long game on utility, not on raw damage. Galio stacks HP and armor into a frontline whose E-into-W taunt and global R win teamfights regardless of your Youmuu burst — and even your R's (Comeuppance) missing-health execute can't reliably chunk a high-HP, armor-stacked target before his taunt locks you. Your job is no longer to win this lane; it's to use your W (Going Rogue) camo and E mobility to splitpush a side and make picks on isolated targets, never grouping into his taunt. If you didn't convert a lead by first item, accept the lane is a wash and play the rest of the map.
